h2: NDT training in Idaho: options across the state compared
html:
NDT training in Idaho: options across the state compared

In our review of Idaho college programme listings for this page, we did not find a dedicated NDT certificate. Idaho State University's energy-systems programmes in Pocatello train nuclear operations, instrumentation and mechanical technicians, and North Idaho College's workforce welding courses stop short of inspection. So an Idaho candidate chooses between an employer that trains on the job, a college programme in a neighbouring state, or online theory with the practical done at work. Which of those is realistic depends heavily on where in the state you live.

Who offers NDT training across Idaho?

  • Treasure Valley: an aviation apprenticeship in Boise. Idaho's training-provider list includes a registered apprenticeship titled Nondestructive Testing, sponsored by Western Aircraft in Boise. The record was last updated in 2021, so ask the company whether it is still running. Its NDT inspector vacancy shows where that path leads: Level 2 in magnetic particle, penetrant, ultrasonic and eddy current to an aerospace standard, after a minimum of eight years in NDT.
  • Pocatello: Idaho State University. ISU's Energy Systems Technology and Education Center trains technicians for utilities and nuclear plants, and its College of Technology lists a civil engineering materials testing certificate. Neither is an NDT method course, but both lead into the plants and contractors that employ NDT people.
  • Eastern Idaho: laboratory and fabrication employers. Contractors and fabricators around the national laboratory hire certified examiners; the Idaho Falls page covers that market in detail.
  • North Idaho: look across the border. Flathead Valley Community College in Kalispell, Montana, describes a Welding and Inspection Technology AAS covering visual, penetrant, magnetic particle, eddy current, ultrasonic and radiographic testing. Clover Park Technical College in Lakewood, Washington, runs an NDT degree plus method certificates. Inland Northwest employers are covered on the Spokane page.
  • Southern Idaho: look to northern Utah. From Pocatello, Twin Falls or Burley, the closest dedicated programmes we verified are Ogden-Weber Technical College's non-destructive inspection course and Salt Lake Community College's NDT degree; see the Ogden page.

Matching an Idaho route to your situation

SituationPractical route in IdahoWatch for
New to NDT in the Treasure ValleyAn assistant role with an aviation or fabrication employer, or an out-of-state programmeWhether the employer certifies to SNT-TC-1A or to an aerospace standard
New to NDT in the PanhandleA Montana or Washington college, or a local employer that trainsMonths of travel or relocation for attendance
Working technician anywhere in the stateOnline theory for the next method plus a practical at your employerHours by method in your written practice
Food, fertiliser, hydro or mining operator with its own crewTraining on your own site with Level III examinationsWho holds the written practice and keeps the records

What to ask an Idaho training provider

  • How far will you travel and for how long? A programme in Kalispell, Lakewood or Ogden can mean months away from home and work.
  • Which document sets the hours: SNT-TC-1A, a customer aerospace standard, or a nuclear quality programme?
  • Is there a practical on real parts with known discontinuities, and who grades it?
  • Who certifies you at the end? Under SNT-TC-1A that is your employer; ASNT certifies only through its own central exams.
  • If radiography is part of your plan, how will you get the radiation-safety training that is required separately from any method course?

Where Atlantis fits for Idaho candidates and employers

Atlantis has no training site anywhere in Idaho, and the course does not need one. Theory for each method is online and self-paced, so a technician in Coeur d'Alene, Boise or Pocatello takes the same course, with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions. The hands-on practical and its examination happen at the employer's own plant or shop under its SNT-TC-1A-based written practice, after rehearsal in the Practical NDT simulator. Course pages: NDT Level 1, NDT Level 2 and ASNT Level III preparation.

For Idaho employers with technicians spread across the state, the more useful step is often a written practice and examinations held on site rather than more travel; see SNT-TC-1A training programme set-up. Common candidate questions are answered in the training FAQ.
